<a id="body"></a>

## Body

Security lesson from #285 at 83e0554bb3d413d0215563fb8774f0dfa4f122e0: an empty-claim shortcut must test absence of all requested-kind pending and running rows, not absence of due or eligible candidates. Delayed, key-blocked and lapsed-running rows still need the full transaction for recovery and expiry. Keep fixed SQL and bind the kind list as JSON data; schema/lease validation and native incarnation/handoff refusals must remain ahead of the shortcut (crates/store/src/queue.rs:96-128,300-303; crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:1844-1855,1993-1994,2146-2152,2209-2215). A second SQLite connection holding BEGIN IMMEDIATE is direct evidence that an empty claim takes no write lock; delayed/key-blocked rows must still attempt the full path. Exact-head CI artifact 14613583362 from successful job 136176117100 in run 44703143649 contains six queue_empty_claim tests, zero skipped/errors/failures. Local shared-build was lock-blocked before Cargo ran; extracted-SQL checks are supplemental, not SQLx integration proof. Preserve these evidence grades when carrying the lesson forward.
